correctness.rationale: From independent domination, each product-cycle fiber is empty, one color, or all colors. The exact local conditions give \(f\) full, \(s\) singleton, \(e\) empty with \(e\le2f+s/2\), hence \(|S|\ge2k+(q-2)f\). For \(q\ge3\) all minima of size \(2k\) have \(f=0\); equality demands one empty fiber in each triple and pairs of equal-colored singletons whose consecutive colors differ. The count is \(3\operatorname{tr}((J_q-I_q)^k)\), eigenvalues \(q-1\) and \(-1\). Different phase zero sets require at least \(k\ge2\) token replacements; fixed-phase color changes require replacing two vertices in a run, so no one-token jump. Standalone code checks the original graph definition exhaustively for \(C_6\times K_3\), \(C_6\times K_4\), \(C_9\times K_3\) (all subsets through optimum size), and word counts and token isolation for seven cases. Infinite claim rests on proof, not computations.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison to Kuenzel--Rall arXiv:2203.12397v1 identifies their Lemma 4, general necessary/sufficient weak-partition description, Proposition 6(c), and constructions of optimal labelings. Those establish the scalar minimum and global general framework. The exact classification of ALL minima at length divisible by three, chromatic cycle multiplicity, and no-single-token-jump reconfiguration are absent from the inspected material, and require an equality-case bound and pairwise-difference argument. The 2023 i-graph article treats individual paths and cycles, not their tensor product; the 2021 two-dominating kernel enumeration is a different stronger predicate with a different minimum size. Actual indexed-result and prior-claim searches found no exact covering statement. Residual priority risk: unindexed or differently formulated literature.

value.rationale: Directly addresses the natural optimizer multiplicity and minimum-solution reconfiguration questions motivated by the established independent domination number and i-graph literature. The theorem supplies a uniform closed exponential count for every alphabet size \(q\ge3\), a rigid extremal equality classification, and an infinite family of isolated minima despite many solutions. The residue-three restriction is dictated by exact tiling equality, not an arbitrary finite slice; these are not merely the old scalar minimum or a relabeling of a published table.
